## How GRACE Follow-On Tracks Water Movement

GRACE Follow-On’s two satellites follow one another about 137 miles (220 kilometers) apart. As they pass a larger mass concentration, gravity affects the leading satellite first, initially increasing the distance between it and the trailing satellite.

Scientists use changes in that separation to infer shifts in mass. Those shifts can help reveal water movement, including changes in groundwater, lakes and rivers, soil moisture, glaciers and ice sheets, and sea level attributable to water added to the oceans.
